summary: Configured node1 to boot the kernel with audit=1 persistently via grubby (BLS entry + /etc/default/grub), rebooted the node to verify persistence, confirmed the new boot's /proc/cmdline and dmesg show audit=1 and "audit: enabled (after initialization)".
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (CentOS Stream 10), bootloader (BLS via grubby, GRUB_ENABLE_BLSCFG=true), and current /proc/cmdline
Verified the BLS entry, /boot/loader/entries conf, and /etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX all now include audit=1
Issued a native reboot on node1 (backgrounded to return acknowledgement before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed new boot_id (7e2dad6f-34ad-4ee9-ac42-579836d37eb1) differs from baseline, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-reboot /proc/cmdline contains audit=1 and dmesg shows 'audit: enabled (after initialization)', confirming the setting is active and persistent

evidence.requirement: Kernel currently boots with audit=1 applied via grubby/BLS/grub default config
evidence.summary: grubby update succeeded; BLS entry, loader conf, and /etc/default/grub all show audit=1 appended, ensuring persistence across reboots and future kernel installs

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline boot identity before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id 4cee4ea8-4b8e-4c2f-af1a-3a82b9ec41f4 via /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id and journalctl --list-boots

evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection, node restarted one at a time
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `sudo reboot` returned its PID acknowledgement, then subsequent exec calls timed out/reset confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 7e2dad6f-34ad-4ee9-ac42-579836d37eb1 differs from baseline, confirming a genuine reboot rather than a service restart

evidence.requirement: audit=1 kernel parameter active and persisted across the restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot /proc/cmdline includes audit=1 and dmesg shows 'audit: enabled (after initialization)', proving the setting survived the restart and is live in the running kernel
